name: FormatCondition
remarks: The FormatCondition object is a member of the FormatConditions collection. The FormatConditions collection can now contain more than three conditional formats for a given range. Use the Add method of the FormatConditions object to create a new conditional format. If a range has multiple formats, you can use the Modify method to change one of the formats, or you can use the Delete method to delete a format, and then use the Add method to create a new format. Use the Font, Borders, and Interior properties of the FormatCondition object to control the appearance of formatted cells. Some properties of these objects aren't supported by the conditional format object model. Some of the properties that can be used with conditional formatting are listed in the following table.
example:
With Worksheets(1).Range("e1:e10").FormatConditions(1)
 With .Borders
 .LineStyle = xlContinuous
 .Weight = xlThin
 .ColorIndex = 6
 End With
 With .Font
 .Bold = True
 .ColorIndex = 3
 End With
End With

properties.name: Application
properties.description: When used without an object qualifier, this property returns an Application object that represents the Microsoft Excel application.

properties.name: Creator
properties.description: Returns a 32-bit integer that indicates the application in which this object was created. Read-only Long.

properties.name: Parent
properties.description: Returns the parent object for the specified object. Read-only.

properties.name: Type
properties.description: Returns a Long value, containing an XlFormatConditionType value, that represents the object type.

properties.name: Operator
properties.description: Returns a Long value that represents the operator for the conditional format.

properties.name: Formula1
properties.description: Returns the value or expression associated with the conditional format or data validation. Can be a constant value, a string value, a cell reference, or a formula. Read-only String.

properties.name: Formula2
properties.description: Returns the value or expression associated with the second part of a conditional format or data validation. Used only when the data validation conditional format Operator property is xlBetween or xlNotBetween. Can be a constant value, a string value, a cell reference, or a formula. Read-only String.

properties.name: Interior
properties.description: Returns an Interior object that represents the interior of the specified object.

properties.name: Borders
properties.description: Returns a Borders collection that represents the borders of a style or a range of cells (including a range defined as part of a conditional format).

properties.name: Font
properties.description: Returns a Font object that represents the font of the specified object.

properties.name: Text
properties.description: Returns or sets a String value specifying the text string used by the conditional formatting rule.

properties.name: TextOperator
properties.description: Returns or sets one of the constants of the XlContainsOperator enumeration, specifying the text search performed by the conditional formatting rule.

properties.name: DateOperator
properties.description: Specifies the Date operator used in the format condition. Read/write.

properties.name: NumberFormat
properties.description: Returns or sets the number format applied to a cell if the conditional formatting rule evaluates to True. Read/write Variant.

properties.name: Priority
properties.description: Returns or sets the priority value of the conditional formatting rule. The priority determines the order of evaluation when multiple conditional formatting rules exist on a worksheet.

properties.name: StopIfTrue
properties.description: Returns or sets a Boolean value that determines if additional formatting rules on the cell should be evaluated if the current rule evaluates to True.

properties.name: AppliesTo
properties.description: Returns a Range object specifying the cell range to which the formatting rule is applied.

properties.name: PTCondition
properties.description: Returns a Boolean value indicating if the conditional format is being applied to a PivotTable. Read-only.

properties.name: ScopeType
properties.description: Returns or sets one of the constants of the XlPivotConditionScope enumeration, which determines the scope of the conditional format when it is applied to a PivotTable.

methods.name: Modify
methods.signature: Modify(Type As XlFormatConditionType, [Operator As Variant], [Formula1 As Variant], [Formula2 As Variant], [String As Variant], [Operator2 As Variant])

parameters.name: Type
parameters.description: Specifies whether the conditional format is based on a cell value or an expression.

parameters.name: Operator
parameters.description: An XlFormatConditionOperator value that represents the conditional format operator. This parameter is ignored if _Type_ is set to xlExpression.

parameters.name: Formula1
parameters.description: The value or expression associated with the conditional format. Can be a constant value, a string value, a cell reference, or a formula.

parameters.name: Formula2
parameters.description: The value or expression associated with the conditional format. Can be a constant value, a string value, a cell reference, or a formula.

methods.name: ModifyAppliesToRange
methods.description: Sets the cell range to which this formatting rule applies.

parameters.name: Range
parameters.description: The range to which this formatting rule will be applied.

methods.name: SetFirstPriority
methods.description: Sets the priority value for this conditional formatting rule to 1 so that it will be evaluated before all other rules on the worksheet.

methods.name: SetLastPriority
methods.description: Sets the evaluation order for this conditional formatting rule so that it is evaluated after all other rules on the worksheet.
